en.title: Last to Be Checked
en.description:
Participants arrive at the times in moments. A single counter checks one person at a time, and each check takes a fixed 300 seconds; if the counter is idle, the check starts immediately, otherwise the person waits. Return the time at which the last participant finishes being checked.

The problem statement and the 300-second duration come from the fixed catalog statement; this site adds the line-based input/output protocol. The original explanation field mistakenly said "300 minutes", which conflicts with the statement's 300 seconds and the example output 1201; following the body text and the examples, this site uses 300 seconds.
en.input: The first line is the number of people n, and the second line contains n space-separated integer arrival times in non-decreasing order. This site's bounds: 1≤n≤100000, 0≤moments[i]≤10^9.
en.output: Output the integer time (in seconds) at which the last participant finishes being checked.
en.explanation: See the accompanying solution for the full approach, correctness proof, and complexity.
hints: Keep track of the time the previous participant finished, and update it person by person.
